AUTHOR: Petrellis
TITLE: Fish Monitoring from Low-Contrast Underwater Images
REGION: Greece (Lampiri, Achaia; Gavathas, Lesvos), shallow Mediterranean coast
SPECIES: Mediterranean seabreams (Diplodus sargus/annularis, Oblada melanura, Pagrus pagrus, others)
DATA: Own UVIMEF dataset (60 videos, 720 photos, low-cost TurboX Act201 camera); 400 frames -> 322 single-fish patches
V_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'captured both during sunny and cloudy days with calm or stormy seas at a depth between 0.5 and 3 m.' Table 10 RMS/Michelson contrast.
D_EV: Sec. 3.1: 'The training of our ERT models has been performed using 270 of these image patches and the rest of them have been used for testing.'
R_EV: Sec. 3.1/4: all training and test patches from UVIMEF; 'The test set of P = 100 fish photographs has been derived from the 52 test photographs'
E_EV: Table 7: 'Fish length error 5.4%' relative to landmark ground truth annotated in the LAE editor on the same images.
ARCH: Pre-trained TF object detector (Faster R-CNN-type, repo [4]) + OpenCV orientation (PCA/COD/FOD/template matching) + Ensemble of Regression Trees (ERT) shape alignment, 18 landmarks
METR: Landmark absolute/relative error, relative length/height error, orientation success rate, latency
NOTE: Platform not stated (low-cost action camera, 0.5-3 m depth; possibly hand-held). Length is RELATIVE length/height vs landmark annotation on the same image, not absolute. Fish detection used an off-the-shelf pre-trained model from [4] with only qualitative/claimed '>95%' detection, training domain of [4] not stated -> R1 coded N (ambiguous; lower-information value). Threshold for COD confidence mentioned without value. Contrast metrics (RMS/Michelson/entropy) computed on 20 photos to compare datasets, not to stratify performance. Data on Kaggle (UVIMEF).
